report.summary: Chunk 4/25 of picker.py: defines CandidateQueue.degraded_sources, NoEvidence, _candidate, WorkQueueInvalid, _project_config, _confined_path, and resolve_spine_db_path. Docstrings contain checkable claims about behavior; several claims about external functions or tests are uncheckable.
risks: _confined_path | medium | Resolves symlinks in parent components, but non-existing leaf files remain valid; this could allow a path that does not exist yet to pass validation and later be created outside the repo root if an intermediate symlink is added after validation. | Verify that the path is checked again at use time (e.g., when opening the file) to ensure it still stays under repo_root.

resolve_spine_db_path | low | Explicitly states it does not read DAEDALUS_SPINE_DB and that this is intentional; if a developer later adds an env var fallback, it would break the contract. | Add a test that ensures DAEDALUS_SPINE_DB is ignored by this function.
todos: Verify that _confined_path is called before any file operation to avoid TOCTOU issues.
Confirm that resolve_spine_db_path is tested with explicit path and project_config combinations.

claims.text: Sources that could NOT be consulted, so an empty queue is explained.
claims.why: The method returns a tuple of source names that are suppressed or have errors, which explains why the queue might be empty.

claims.text: "The source was withheld or unreadable" and "the sources are healthy and there is no work" are different facts, and a caller that cannot tell them apart will eventually read a broken adapter as "nothing to do" -- which is the quiet failure this whole queue exists to avoid.
claims.why: The method distinguishes degraded sources (suppressed/error) from healthy ones, allowing callers to differentiate.

claims.text: Everything here is already visible in ``sources``/``notes`` for a human; this is the same fact in a shape a program can branch on.
claims.why: The claim about sources/notes being visible to humans refers to other attributes of the class not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: A candidate was constructed without a reason or without evidence.
claims.why: NoEvidence is raised by _candidate when reason or evidence is missing.

claims.text: Construct a candidate, refusing one that carries no evidence.
claims.why: _candidate raises NoEvidence if reason or evidence is empty or missing.

claims.text: The refusal is a raise, not a skip: an evidence-free candidate is a bug in a source function, and silently dropping it would hide the bug while the queue quietly got shorter.
claims.why: The function raises NoEvidence, which will propagate and not be silently dropped.

claims.text: The enabled queue exists, but cannot safely drive an attempt.
claims.why: No code in this chunk uses WorkQueueInvalid; it is defined but not raised here.

claims.text: Resolve a configured path and prove it stays under ``repo_root``.
claims.why: The function resolves the path and checks it is relative to repo_root, raising WorkQueueInvalid if not.

claims.text: ``Path.resolve`` follows an existing symlink in any parent component, so a lexically innocent ``.agentenv/link/queue.json`` cannot escape through a junction/symlink.
claims.why: The code uses .resolve() on both root and candidate, which follows symlinks.

claims.text: Non-existing leaf files remain valid, which is necessary to distinguish an enabled-but-ABSENT source from an INVALID path.
claims.why: The function does not check file existence; it only resolves and checks containment.

claims.text: The historical default lived under agent_env even when ``repo_root`` named another repository. That split the loop: the writer recorded PnP attempts while the picker remembered agent_env attempts. The default is now ``<repo>/runs/spine/spine.sqlite3`` and a configured override is accepted only when its resolved target remains inside that same repository.
claims.why: The default path and historical behavior are not implemented in this chunk; only the function signature and docstring are present.

claims.text: DELIBERATELY DOES NOT READ ``DAEDALUS_SPINE_DB``, and this is the ruling, not an oversight (resolver author, 2026-07-29): that env var belongs to the process-global ledger surface -- :func:`daedalus.spine.ledger.default_db_path` -- where tests and isolated worktrees point the WHOLE process elsewhere.
claims.why: The function body is not shown; the claim about not reading the env var cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.why: The reference to tests/test_picker_work_queue.py is outside this chunk.
